dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Lunar Rover is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Lunar Rover has shown intense fearful behavior, including trembling, a tucked and tense body, whale eye, hard staring, flinching away from handlers, avoiding leashing and handling, and refusing treats. She has also shown head whipping and increased tension during leash removal. Lunar Rover continues to struggle to acclimate to the shelter environment and remains fearful and avoidant during interactions with handlers. Lunar Rover's previous owners report her to be social, affectionate, active, playful, and vocal. Medically, Lunar Rover is receiving treatment for CIRDC. Lunar Rover also has a mammary gland tumor that need removal and biopsy.

Lunar Rover was surrendered by her previous owner due to owner circumstances. With her family, she is a social, affectionate, active, playful, vocal, and fearful dog. She spends most of her time where people are, in the living room, and in the backyard. Lunar Rover enjoys car rides, but does whine throughout; she enjoys hikes and sunbathing. Lunar Rover has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.
